name: Harbin Taiping International Airport
before:
The largest airport in Heilongjiang and the main hub for north east China, about 37 km south west of Harbin. It handled 24,650,717 passengers in 2025, twenty second in mainland China, across 97 destinations of which 85 are domestic.

The two terminals are separate buildings about a mile apart, which is the single most important thing to tell a connecting client. Terminal 2, opened in April 2018, takes domestic flights only. All international flights use the older terminal to the north, which is being redeveloped for the purpose. Allow real time to move between them.

A second runway opened in January 2025, giving the airport a 3,200 metre and a 3,600 metre runway side by side.

The airport was built in 1979 as Yanjiagang, replacing the old Majiagou airfield the Japanese had built in 1931, and took international status in 1984 with flights to Russia.
after:
The largest airport in Heilongjiang and an important hub for north east China, about 37 km south west of Harbin. It handled 24.65 million passengers in 2025, the 22nd busiest in mainland China. Its summer 2026 schedule serves 95 destinations, 83 of them in mainland China.

All international flights have used a rebuilt Terminal 1 since July 2024. It is joined to Terminal 2, so international and domestic connections are made under one roof. Terminal 2, opened in April 2018, is for domestic flights.

A second runway opened in January 2025, giving the airport a 3,200 metre and a 3,600 metre runway side by side.

The airport was built in 1979 as Yanjiagang, replacing the old Majiagou airfield.

claims.note: Harbin TV reports it was the busiest airport in the whole of north east China in 2022 to 2024, which covers Heilongjiang; it also carries 3,440 of the Heilongjiang Airport Group's 4,339 weekly flights in summer 2026.

claims.wasBefore: Allow real time to move between them.

claims.claim: Majiagou built by the Japanese in 1931
claims.why: No second source. The Paper's history describes Majiagou only from 1950, as a shared military and civil field.

claims.claim: international status in 1984 with flights to Russia
claims.wasBefore: and took international status in 1984 with flights to Russia
claims.why: Sources disagree on the date: Spring Airlines says scheduled international flights began in 1984 but international status came with the 1998 renaming; The Paper says it opened to foreign traffic on 1 July 1987. 'Russia' would have been the Soviet Union in 1984.
